evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (CUHK Chinese Lexical Database)
evidence.field: 告: 形義通解、字例、廣韻讀音
evidence.text: CUHK reports Zhang Yujin’s proposal that oracle-bone 告 differentiates from 舌 by extending its central stroke upward, depicting a mouth with a protruding tongue and relating to speaking or telling. It also records the 牛+口 sacrificial interpretation as an alternative. Cited examples include a Shang oracle-bone use as a sacrificial name read 祰 (合集1166甲), a report about a deer (屯南997), Western Zhou bronze uses for reporting, admonishing and accusation, and a Warring States slip use for telling. These examples do not establish a linear semantic chronology. CUHK lists Guangyun readings 古到 and 古沃.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫

evidence.field: File description, provenance and reuse license
evidence.text: The page identifies this as a modern vector drawing of the Shuowen Jiezi Lesser Seal form, made by LiliCharlie on 2013-12-09 and manually straightened. It is own work, licensed CC BY-SA 3.0; reuse requires attribution, a license link and indication of changes, with share-alike for adaptations. It is a representation of a received seal-script form, not an ancient artifact photograph.

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: A00528 告; 說文釋形、字樣說明、readings and senses
evidence.text: The dictionary reproduces the Shuowen explanation of an ox striking a person with its horns restrained by a crossbar and analyzes the graph as 口 plus 牛. It describes the seal form in that account and provides later readings and senses, including reporting, requesting, accusation/litigation and leave. These dictionary entries do not date the first occurrence of each sense or independently verify the Shu-period analysis for Shang forms.
evidence.title: [A00528] 告 - 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.text: The Japanese Wiktionary file page describes 告-oracle.svg as a modern vector depiction of 告 in oracle script style, cites several reference databases and an image identifier, and states the redraw is released to the public domain. This is description-page evidence, not visual inspection of the glyph pixels or confirmation that the depicted form is representative of a specific artifact.

search_audit.query: site:commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File "告-oracle.svg"; "File:告-oracle.svg" Commons; "File:告-bronze.svg" Commons; 告-oracle.svg Commons
search_audit.outcome: Commons category verified candidate filenames. Exact oracle and bronze Commons description pages returned cache misses, but Japanese Wiktionary’s mirrored file-description pages were searchable and provided description and license text for oracle and big-seal candidates.

Exact Commons file pages and MediaWiki imageinfo API were attempted; they returned cache-miss or inaccessible errors. Subsequent search located mirrored descriptions for oracle and big-seal candidates, but not bronze.

gaps: No direct image URL was selected: Commons description-page search snippets and mirrored file descriptions did not expose a verified original-image URL, and direct original-file/API attempts were inaccessible. The harness should not receive a guessed upload URL.

The direct Commons description pages for 告-oracle.svg and 告-bronze.svg returned cache misses. Their file descriptions and exact original image links were not independently checked on Commons in this session; mirrored metadata for 告-oracle.svg is not a substitute for verifying the direct original URL.

The disputed early form analysis remains unresolved among the protruding-tongue/舌 account, Shuowen’s 牛+口 explanation, and the reported 壴+口 proposal. No graph pixels were visually inspected in this stage.

CUHK’s cited Shang oracle-bone, Western Zhou bronze and Warring States examples were not checked against original artifact images or independently dated here. Their reported senses cannot establish a chronological chain of semantic extensions.
The exact Unicode Unihan record for 告 remained inaccessible. The supplied local row is not external confirmation.
No independent component phonetic claim is established by these sources; the graphic proposals treat 口 as pictorial/semantic or do not identify a secure phonetic element.

items.period: Shuowen Jiezi Lesser Seal tradition; modern vector file dated 2013-12-09
items.tradition: Small/Lesser Seal (小篆), Shuowen Jiezi radical form
items.caption: Modern vector redraw of the 告 seal form transmitted in the Shuowen Jiezi tradition; it illustrates the later lexicographic form, not the disputed Shang graph origin.
items.alt: Modern outlined seal-script form of 告 from a Shuowen radical redraw.
items.selection_reason: The exact Commons page identifies the item as Shuowen Lesser Seal script and records an explicit license. It gives a useful later comparison point for a dossier whose competing analyses concern earlier forms.
items.rights: CC BY-SA 3.0; attribute the creator, link the license, indicate changes, and share adaptations under compatible terms.

limitations.text: No direct image candidate was selected for Shang oracle or bronze forms. Commons lists 告-oracle.svg and 告-bronze.svg, but their exact Commons file pages and original-image URLs were inaccessible; mirrored oracle metadata did not provide a verified direct image URL. No glyph pixels were visually inspected.
